name: China
headline: China: +5.0% growth in 2025, 0.0% inflation, debt 99% of GDP
sections: China is a $19.63 trillion economy (2025), the world's 3rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.0% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $29K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 24.7% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.1% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 99% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 71% in 2020. The general government balance is −7.9% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +3.7% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 38% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 122% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 78.0 years (2024). Population: 1404.9 million (2025).
